info.title: wgate
info.description: Multi-tenant WireGuard gateway: portal API. The `/auth` paths are at the root, not under `/api/v1`.

get.summary: Newest first, a page at a time.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Entries older than this id (the previous page's last).

get.summary:
A live link's account and purpose; 404 for any other token (unknown, used,
expired, voided, or an invite for an account that has a password by now). Limited per client as login attempts are.

post.summary:
Sets the account's password and uses the link up; a reset link also ends the
account's sessions and clears its lockouts. No session: log in next. 404 as for
the `GET`, 422 for a password out of bounds, 429/503 as for a login.

The enabled global providers and, for an existing account of a tenant, that
tenant's. An unknown email gets what an account without tenant providers gets:
the page reveals only which tenant an account is in, and only when that tenant
has its own provider.

204 with the session cookie, or 401 `invalid_credentials` for any failure. The
session's `stage` (`GET /api/v1/session`) says what is next: `totp` for an
account with TOTP on (`POST /auth/totp`), `enrol` for an admin without it, else
`full`. 429
(with `Retry-After`) after 20 attempts a minute from one client or 100 from one
IPv6 /48; 503 `busy` when every hashing slot stays taken for 2 s.

204.description: Signed in: the session cookie is set

post.summary:
Only for a session in the `totp` stage (5 minutes from the password), with its
`X-CSRF-Token` (from `GET /api/v1/session`). 204 with a new session cookie for the
now `full` session; 401 `invalid_credentials` for any failure (the session stays
for another try until it expires, or until the client is locked out: then it
ends), 401 `unauthorized` without such a session; 400 unless exactly one of
`code` and `recovery_code`; 403 without the CSRF token; 429 (with `Retry-After`)
as for `/auth/password`, or when the account's next code attempt is more than
30 s away (attempts since the last right code are spaced out: the first two at
once, then 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, … at most 5 minutes apart; a reply may take up to 30 s).

204.description: Signed in: a new session cookie is set

delete.summary: Takes the block's networks (and their peers) along.
Rules it no longer covers drop out of the next compile (fail closed).

post.summary: Between networks of two different tenants (the schema refuses one tenant).

get.summary: A free block of `prefix` in the pool (clear of reserved space and routed LANs).

delete.summary:
Unlinks one of the account's identities, and ends its other sessions made through
that provider. 422 if it is the last way in (no password, no other identity at
an enabled provider).

post.summary:
Starts linking an identity at provider `id` to the signed-in account: an
enabled provider that serves it (a tenant's provider only its own tenant's
accounts). 404 for no such (enabled) provider, 403 for one that does not serve the
account, 409 if the account has an identity there already, 503 `unavailable` when
the provider cannot be reached (the cause is in the server's log).

Needs the current password. A wrong one counts like a failed login from this
client: 422 while attempts remain, then 429 (with `Retry-After`) during the
lockout. 422 for an account without a password, 503 `busy` as for a login. Ends
every other session of the account.

204.description: Changed; the other sessions are over

get.summary:
The enabled providers the signed-in account may link, any role: the global ones
and its tenant's.

post.summary:
Needs a current TOTP code, counted like a login attempt (422 when wrong, then
429): ten new recovery codes, the old ones void. 422 with TOTP off.

delete.summary:
Needs the current password, counted like a login attempt as for a password
change (422 when wrong, then 429). Admins may not: they need TOTP (422). Removes
the recovery codes too.

post.summary:
Turns the pending secret on with one of its codes: the recovery codes. In the
`enrol` stage the session becomes `full` under a new cookie (audited as the
enrolment). 422 for a wrong code (or none pending); not counted as a login
attempt: it checks the secret the setup just handed out.

A new secret, pending until `/me/totp/confirm` (a pending one is replaced). In a
`full` session it takes the current password, counted like a login attempt as
for a password change (422 when wrong, then 429); the `enrol` stage sends no
body. 409 with TOTP on; 422 for an account without a password.
Inside one of its tenant's blocks; slug, range and port are the network's for good.

delete.summary: Takes the network's peers, routes, rules, federations and grants along.

get.summary: A free peer address in the network.

post.summary: Sources outside tenant space only (inside it, federations decide).

An external rule must lie inside the tenant's ceiling: 422 with what is not
covered. A network target is one of the same tenant's.
Final: its address, key and LANs are free again.

409 for a name already on the same login page; 422 for a malformed issuer, an
empty field, or `link_by_email` on a tenant's provider.

delete.summary:
Takes its identities along (an account left without a way in needs an invite
link) and ends the sessions made through it; audited with how many. 409 when an
admin account would be left without a way in, unless a global admin asks.

patch.summary:
403/409/422 as for a create. A new issuer drops the provider's identities (its
subjects were the old issuer's); that and disabling end the sessions made through
it, and answer with `stranded`: the accounts left without a way in. 409 when one
of those is an admin account, unless a global admin asks.

get.summary: Any role, any stage; only admins may use the rest of the API.

delete.summary:
Takes everything of the tenant along: blocks, networks, users, devices, peers,
rules, ceilings.

post.summary:
A block of the pool (never reserved space); the schema keeps blocks and routed
LANs disjoint.
What a tenant's networks may be granted outside tenant space.

get.summary: A free range of `prefix` in the tenant's blocks (or in one of them).

parameters.name: block_id
parameters.description: Only inside this block of the tenant's.

delete.summary: Takes the user's devices and peers along.

get.summary:
An account's identities, as far as invite and reset links reach (a tenant admin
their tenant's plain users, a global admin anyone; one's own: `/me`).

post.summary:
Pre-links an identity: its next login through that provider is this account. As
far as invite and reset links reach (a tenant admin their tenant's plain users, a
global admin anyone, nobody their own account: 422). The provider must serve the
account (422 otherwise); 409 if the subject is another account's or the account
has an identity there already.

delete.summary:
Unlinks an identity of an account in reach (as for a pre-link), and ends the
account's sessions made through that provider. 422 for the last way in.

post.summary:
A link to set the first password of an account that has none (409 if it has
one: send a reset link). Voids the account's older links. 403 out of reach (a
tenant admin: their tenant's plain users only), 422 for your own account.

A link to set a new password; following it also ends the account's sessions and
clears its lockouts. Voids the account's older links. 403/404/422 as for an
invite.

Turns the account's TOTP off (with its recovery codes) and ends its sessions: its
next password login sets TOTP up again (an admin's must). 403/404/422 as for an
invite.

204.description: TOTP is off; the account's sessions are over

url.description: `<public_url>/account/<token>`, for the account's owner. Shown this once.

ErrorBody.description: The JSON body of every error.

detail.description: What is in the way (e.g. the part of a rule no ceiling covers).

subject.description: The provider's subject identifier for the account.
The provider's subject identifier (`sub`) for the account's owner.

warnings.description: E.g. a source so broad that every target peer becomes a full tunnel.

email.description: The account the link is for.

url.description:
Send the browser here (the provider's login); it comes back to `/me`, with
`?linked=<provider id>` or `?error=` (`taken`: the identity is another
account's; `exists`, `forbidden`, `expired`, `cancelled`, `unavailable`,
`failed`). Only this browser, in this session, can finish it.

global.description: A global provider (else the account's tenant's own).

linked.description: Whether the account has an identity there already (then unlink it first).

providers.description: Sign in through one of these at `GET /auth/oidc/{id}`.

hub_public_key.description: Published by the agent once the network is up.

mesh.description: Members may reach each other without a rule.

disabled.description: Disabling takes the interface down at once (reversible).

routes.description: The LANs it routes (active routes only).

public_key.description: The device's own public key; omitted, the server makes the pair.

oneOf.description: With the private key: the only time a server key is shown.

identities.description: How many accounts have linked an identity there.

managed.description:
Whether the caller manages it; a tenant admin sees a global provider's name
only (the fields below are then `None`).

stranded.description:
In an update's answer only: how many accounts it left without a way to log
in (they need an invite link).

link_by_email.description: A first login binds by verified email (global providers, global admins only).

name.description: On the login button; unique among the providers of the same login page.

tenant_id.description: `None` makes a global provider (a global admin's call only).

id.description: The provider's id, as a string (opaque to the login page).

stranded.description:
How many accounts the delete left without a way to log in (they need an
invite link).

client_secret.description: Write-only; left out, the stored one stays.

disabled.description: Disabling ends the sessions made through it; nobody logs in or links there.

issuer.description: A new issuer is another provider's subjects: its identities go.

recovery_codes.description: Ten single-use codes for when the authenticator is gone. Shown this once.

qr_svg.description:
The same as a QR code (SVG) for the WireGuard app; missing when the config is
too long for one.

ServiceBody.description: Protocol and ports of a rule-like row.

csrf.description: Send it back as `X-CSRF-Token` on every write.

has_password.description: Whether the account has a password (to change; TOTP needs one).

stage.description:
How far the login got: `totp` waits for `POST /auth/totp`, `enrol` for the
TOTP setup (`/me/totp/setup`, `/me/totp/confirm`); only `full` uses the API.

totp_enabled.description: Whether TOTP is on (not merely set up).

password.description:
The current password; not needed right after a password login (the `enrol`
stage of one).

applied_revision.description: What the agent last applied (behind `revision` while it catches up).

error.description:
What the agent could not apply, if anything: its own words (every tenant's
interfaces and ranges), so for a global admin only.

failing.description: Whether the agent reported an error.

disabled.description: Disabling cuts every network of the tenant off at once (reversible).

recovery_code.description: One of the account's recovery codes, instead (each works once).

otpauth_uri.description: For an authenticator app; holds the secret. Shown this once.

qr_svg.description: The same as a QR code.

has_password.description: Whether it has a password (then an invite is refused: send a reset link).

stranded.description:
In an update's answer only, when a promotion took identities at tenant
providers away: whether that left the account without a way in (send an
invite link).

tenant_id.description: `None` makes a global admin (a global admin's call only).

disabled.description: Disabling ends their sessions and takes their peers out at once (reversible).
